fields.description:
Every citation below describes the tree at commit `60bd5ec`, the base this work branches from.

ADP is a general-purpose platform. A repository it is piloted against must not appear in its committed configuration.

At `60bd5ec`, `compose.override.yaml` was tracked and named a client repository four times. It mounted `../archive-massgov-pfml` into the activity worker and, read-only, into the repository-intelligence services, and registered that repository in two `REPO_INTELLIGENCE_REPOS` values. A comment named the client product. Those entries sat beside the platform's own `agentic-demo-*` mounts, which belong there.

At `60bd5ec`, `config/local/checks.yaml` was tracked while every other operator-edited config in that directory was not. `.gitignore` establishes the convention that the platform ships a `.yaml.example` template and ignores the operator's `.yaml`, applied to `github`, `jira`, `integrations`, `gates`, `gate_engine`, `tickets`, and `review-trust-root`. `checks.yaml` shipped an example but had no ignore pair, so it was committed. The operator's copy carried a client entry and was held back only by a `skip-worktree` bit, which also hides local edits from `git status`.

At `60bd5ec`, project compose overlays had no ignore rule. The pilot overlay was excluded through `.git/info/exclude`, which lives outside the repository and protects one checkout. A fresh clone has no such protection.

At `60bd5ec`, `README.md` and `tests/unit/test_intake_base.py` carried `base:joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758`, a personal account name with a client ticket key. Two committed artefacts carried a maintainer's home directory, `services/repository_intelligence/eval/scorecards/agentic-demo-service@0744a6e.2026-07-27.json` in its gold and toolchain provenance and `tests/fixtures/scip/agentic-demo-service@0744a6e.scip.json` in its project root. `services/repository_intelligence/eval/harness.py` wrote those absolute paths and defaulted its corpus and binary locations to one maintainer's directory layout, so regenerating an artefact reintroduced the leak.

Client repository names also appear as sample values in nine test fixtures. Those encode no client behaviour and are out of scope here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No tracked file names the client repository, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k no_tracked_file_names_a_client_repository`
- [ ] No tracked file carries an absolute home directory path, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k no_tracked_file_carries_a_personal_account_path`
- [ ] Every operator-edited config that ships an example is ignored, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k every_operator_config_is_ignored_and_has_an_example`
- [ ] A project compose overlay is ignored, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k project_compose_overlays_are_ignored`
- [ ] The platform's own compose files stay tracked, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_hygiene.py -k the_platform_compose_files_stay_tracked`
- [ ] The documented base branch example uses a neutral account, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_base.py -k slashed_branch_is_preserved`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
